lyrics:
[Intro: drum fill, sparkling fast synth riff]

[Verse 1: low soft vocal, riff drops out, bass and pad]
Three dots on the glass, then they disappear
I've been writing you all year
Every word's a paper plane
Folded twice and thrown away again

[Pre-Chorus: rising pad, tom build]
I'm no good at standing still
If I don't jump now, I never will

[Chorus: melody climbs step by step into falsetto]
Say me yes (say me yes)
Say it now (say it now)
I'm a sketch 'til you color me in somehow
Say me yes
One word and I'm real
Say me, say me yes

[Verse 2: low soft vocal]
You talk like there's forever in your coat
I'm a candle on a boat
Shy is just a slower kind of brave
Watch me learn it wave by wave

[Pre-Chorus: rising pad, tom build]
I'm no good at standing still
If I don't jump now, I never will

[Chorus: climbs into falsetto, echoed backing vocals]
Say me yes (say me yes)
Say it now (say it now)
I'm a sketch 'til you color me in somehow
Say me yes
One word and I'm real
Say me, say me yes

[Bridge: stripped back, new chord colour]
Oh, the things we never send
Pile up like snow against the door
Open it, open it
I can't hold it anymore

[Synth Solo: lead riff with pitch bends]

[Breakdown Chorus: kick and claps only, sung gently]
Say me yes (say me yes)
Say it slow (say it slow)
I was only ever waiting for a go

[Final Chorus: full power, last note held in high falsetto]
Say me yes (say me yes)
Say it now (say it now)
I'm a sketch 'til you color me in somehow
Say me yes
One word and I'm real
Say me, say me yes
Say me, say me yes

[Outro: synth riff, echoing vocal, hard stop]
(Yes, yes, yes)
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 166 BPM, 4/4, B major (verses hover on the relative minor, the chorus bursts into the major). Fast, bright, nervous energy, like a heartbeat before a first kiss.

VOICE: Male voice with a huge range. Verses sit low, soft and slightly accented, nearly mumbled. Each chorus line steps higher until the last 'yes' is held in clear, pure falsetto at the very top of the range. Echoed backing answers in the chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A sparkling staccato synth lead playing a fast, bouncing riff (bright digital bell tone layered with a warm analog saw). Octave-jumping synth bass. Crisp drum machine with a cracking snare and sixteenth-note hi-hats. Strummed acoustic guitar tucked underneath for lift. Soft string pad in the pre-chorus. Tom fills into each chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, a drum fill then the full synth riff for 8 bars. 0:14 Verse 1, the riff drops out leaving bass, drums and a held pad. 0:37 Pre-chorus, rising pad and tom build. 0:49 Chorus 1, three steps upward. 1:12 Riff returns. 1:24 Verse 2. 1:47 Pre-chorus. 1:59 Chorus 2. 2:22 Bridge, half the instruments and a new chord colour. 2:45 Synth solo over the riff with pitch bends. 3:08 Breakdown chorus, kick and claps only, sung gently. 3:20 Final chorus at full power, the last 'yes' held for 4 bars. 3:50 Outro, riff and echoing 'yes', hard stop at 4:00.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Glossy and bright. Wide chorus on the synths, a gated reverb snare, vocal dry in the verses and drenched in plate reverb on the high notes.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The final held falsetto 'yes', a note placed just out of reach of the average singer so every crowd attempts it and laughs.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: A wide modern super-saw layer and gentle side-chain pumping join for the final chorus only. The intro riff is doubled by a soft 'typing' tick pattern.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Shy, then brave, then airborne.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

Someone shy has spent a year writing and deleting the same message. Tonight they finally ask: one word from you and I stop being a sketch and become real.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a crush finally confessed; a job, a move or a dream waiting on someone's approval; a kid asking a parent to believe in them; or a person coming out and asking to be accepted. 'Three dots on the glass' is a typing indicator to one generation and rain on a window to another.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: a deliberately off-grammar title that becomes a catchphrase, low murmured verses nobody will learn, and a chorus that climbs to a note the crowd will miss together. Designed mishearing: 'Say me yes' is heard as 'Save me, yes', which means the same thing and deepens it.
